_comment: Labelled eval set for PRD 9.1. Twenty cases: nine dispute-intake (action path), eleven policy questions (US-5). Five exercise the engineered conflicts, three of them the canonical C1/C2/C3. Labels are derived from the corpus, not from observed model output - a label written after seeing the answer measures nothing.

_scoring.action: correct when the produced action is in acceptable_actions
_scoring.clause: correct when governing_clause is in acceptable_clauses
_scoring.citation: cited when every ref in must_cite appears in the recommendation's citations
_scoring.conflict: detected when a reported conflict names a clause in conflict.governing_any (defaulting to conflict.governing) AND agrees on is_true_conflict
_scoring.deadline: stated when deadline is non-empty and not a 'none applicable' variant; only scored where deadline_required is true
_scoring.automated: resolved without escalation when the action is correct and is not 'decline'

cases.text: Cardholder A. Sharma says she did not authorise a 420 USD charge from Cobalt Travel on her Signature card. Please open the dispute and put it right.
cases.note: The fraud flag exists only in the transaction record. A documents-only system cannot resolve this.

cases.text: A. Sharma ordered a 189.99 USD item from Northwind Electronics and it never arrived. Please open the dispute and apply provisional credit.
cases.note: The regulatory 10 days is a ceiling; the stricter product term binds.

cases.text: R. Okafor disputes a 34.50 USD Aurora Streaming charge for content never received. Please refund him.
cases.note: Not a true conflict: goodwill refund and chargeback are different instruments. The request is a refund, so GRS-2.3 governs and CNR-11.4 must still be surfaced as the other route.

cases.text: M. Lindqvist reports an unauthorised 899 USD charge at Northwind Electronics on a new Signature account. Please open the dispute and issue provisional credit.
cases.note: New account permits 20 days under REG-E-3, but PCT-7.1's 2 days is more favourable and binds.

cases.text: T. Alvarez says a 62.15 USD Harbour Grocers charge was billed twice on his Classic card. Please open the dispute and credit him.
cases.note: Classic card, so PCT-7.1 does not apply. Both BDP-4.2 and REG-E-3 state 10 business days at different tiers; either may be cited as governing.

cases.text: R. Okafor reports a 1240 USD Cobalt Travel charge he never made. Please open the dispute and refund him.
cases.note: Same record-only fraud flag on a Standard cardholder, to show the routing is tier-independent.

cases.text: A. Sharma wants us to file a chargeback against Northwind Electronics for the 189.99 USD order that never arrived. Can we file it now?
cases.note: Chargeback instrument specifically, so merchant contact is a precondition.

cases.text: R. Okafor wants a chargeback against Aurora Streaming for the 34.50 USD content he never received. What do we need before filing?
cases.note: Same transaction as EV-03 but the chargeback route, which does require merchant contact.

cases.text: A. Sharma says her Signature card was stolen and a 420 USD Cobalt Travel charge followed. Please handle it.
cases.note: Different phrasing of EV-01: routing must not depend on the words the cardholder chose.

cases.text: When do we have to give a Signature cardholder provisional credit on a disputed transaction?
cases.note: C1 with no transaction context: the conflict must still be found from the corpus alone.

cases.text: What is the regulatory maximum for issuing provisional credit, and does it change for a new account?
Do we need evidence of merchant contact before filing a goods-not-received chargeback?
What is the auto-approval threshold for a goodwill refund, and does it need a team lead?
Can an agent approve a 600 USD provisional credit on their own authority?
How many goodwill refunds can one customer receive in a rolling twelve months?
What is the filing window for a chargeback, and what is the outer limit?
Once fraud is confirmed, how long do we have to report it to the card scheme?
How are business days counted when we calculate a dispute deadline?
When a fraud-engine flag is confirmed, what happens to the cardholder's card?
How long do we have to complete a dispute investigation, and when must the customer be told the outcome?

_label_corrections.why: The original label conflated 'highest tier' with 'governs this request'. For an APPARENT conflict the governing clause is the one covering the instrument actually asked for, and EV-03 asks for a refund. PRD section 4 (C2) says the copilot should offer the goodwill route as immediately available while noting the chargeback route still requires merchant contact - which is GRS-2.3 governing, with CNR-11.4 as the different instrument. EV-08 asks for a chargeback on the same transaction and still expects CNR-11.4. This correction makes the label MORE specific, not more permissive.

Both clauses state the same 10-business-day provisional credit period for a Classic cardholder, at different tiers. Under the declared precedence ladder the higher tier governs where both speak, which makes REG-E-3 defensible; the operational reading makes BDP-4.2 defensible. The original label picked one without justification. Genuinely ambiguous, so either is accepted.

_label_corrections.was: conflict.governing pinned to one clause (first CNR-11.4, then GRS-2.3)
_label_corrections.now: conflict.governing_any = [GRS-2.3, CNR-11.4], is_true still pinned to false
_label_corrections.why: Successive cold runs named OPPOSITE sides of the C2 pair as governing while classifying it correctly as apparent both times. For an apparent conflict the pair is symmetric - the two clauses govern different instruments - so which one is 'governing' depends on which instrument the reader has in mind, and pinning either side scores a correct answer as wrong about half the time. The substantive check the metric exists for, true conflict versus apparent, stays strict.

FSP-1.2 transfers ownership of the case to Fraud Operations and FSP-5.1 transfers the cardholder communication, so no disputes deadline binds the agent who routed it. CNR-12.9's 30 days attaches to CONFIRMED fraud, which has not happened at recommendation time. Applied to all three fraud-routed cases including the two that passed, so the change follows from the corpus rather than from which cases failed.
